streets.name: Vicus Iovis Fagutalis
streets.modern: Fagutal (west Oppius), near Via delle Sette Sale (conjectural)
streets.note: Street on the Fagutal named after the shrine of Jupiter Fagutalis (beech grove), known from an inscription of AD 109 (CIL VI 452).

streets.name: Road from the Colosseum to the Lateran along the north slope of the Caelian
streets.modern: Via dei Santi Quattro
streets.note: Line of Via dei Santi Quattro from the Ludus Magnus area to the Lateran past the Castra Peregrina side; medieval route on probably ancient alignment.

streets.name: Vicus Frumentarius (conjectural)
streets.modern: Emporium district between the Porticus Aemilia and the Horrea Galbana
streets.note: Street of Region XIII among the warehouses below the Aventine, the home of grain dealers (Capitoline Base; Platner); placed between the Porticus Aemilia and the Horrea Galbana.

streets.name: Street along the Horrea Galbana
streets.modern: Via Nicola Zabaglia (approx.)
streets.note: Street skirting the Horrea Galbana (Sulpicii Galbae, later imperial) in Testaccio; drawn on Via Nicola Zabaglia.

streets.name: Clivus Capsarius
streets.modern: Via di Santa Prisca (conjectural)
streets.note: Street 'in Aventino maiore' (Acta Arvalia, AD 240), perhaps named from the capsarii, the cloakroom attendants of the Baths of Caracalla, who lived there (Platner).

streets.name: Lane of the Vatican necropolis (under St Peter's)
streets.modern: Scavi under the nave of St Peter's
streets.note: East-west lane between the mausolea of the necropolis north of the Via Cornelia, ending at the 'Campo P' with the aedicula over St Peter's grave; buried by Constantine's basilica (c. 320).
scholarship: Liverani and Spinola, The Vatican Necropoles (2010)

streets.name: Via Collatina (outside the Porta Maggiore)
streets.modern: from the Praenestina east-north-east (approx.)
streets.note: Road to Collatia, branching from the Praenestina just outside the Porta Maggiore (Platner, Via Collatina); course in the model area approximate.

streets.name: Road along the northern Campus Martius toward the Mausoleum of Augustus
streets.modern: Via di Ripetta
streets.note: North-south road between the Mausoleum of Augustus and the river bank toward the Porta Flaminia district, on the line of Via di Ripetta.
scholarship: Haselberger et al., Mapping Augustan Rome (2002)

streets.name: Street along the north side of the Saepta Iulia
streets.modern: Via del Seminario
streets.note: East-west street between the Saepta Iulia and the Temple of Matidia / Hadrianeum area, on the line of Via del Seminario.
scholarship: Haselberger et al., Mapping Augustan Rome (2002)

streets.name: Street between the Saepta Iulia and the Iseum
streets.modern: Via del Gesù - Via di S. Ignazio line
streets.note: North-south street on the east side of the Saepta Iulia (Diribitorium) beside the Iseum Campense.
scholarship: Haselberger et al., Mapping Augustan Rome (2002)

streets.name: Street between the Pantheon / Baths of Agrippa and the Saepta
streets.modern: Via dei Cestari - Via della Minerva
streets.note: North-south street east of the Pantheon and Baths of Agrippa, between them and the Saepta, on the line of Via dei Cestari and Via della Minerva.
scholarship: Haselberger et al., Mapping Augustan Rome (2002)

streets.name: Street round the cavea of the Theatre of Pompey
streets.modern: Via di Grotta Pinta - Via dei Chiavari
streets.note: Medieval streets that follow the curve of the theatre's substructures (Via di Grotta Pinta, Via dei Chiavari) keep the line of the passage round the outside of the cavea.

streets.name: Street west of the Area Sacra of Largo Argentina
streets.modern: Via di Torre Argentina
streets.note: North-south street along the west side of the Area Sacra between the temples and the Hecatostylon / Curia of Pompey, on the line of Via di Torre Argentina.

streets.name: Street from the Ripa to the Via Aurelia (Trastevere)
streets.modern: Via di San Francesco a Ripa
streets.note: Cross-street of Trastevere from the river harbour toward S. Maria in Trastevere, on Via di S. Francesco a Ripa.

streets.name: Vicus Bellonae (conjectural)
streets.modern: by the Theatre of Marcellus and the Temple of Bellona
streets.note: Probably named from the Temple of Bellona in the Campus Martius by the Circus Flaminius; known from one inscription (CIL VI 2235).

streets.name: Vicus Laci Fundani
streets.modern: Quirinal, near Via della Dataria (conjectural)
streets.note: Street named from the Lacus Fundanus on the Quirinal (Capitoline Base); position approximate.

streets.name: Vicus Padi (conjectural)
streets.modern: east slope of the Palatine toward the Arch of Constantine
streets.note: Street of Region X (Capitoline Base), probably on the eastern slope of the Palatine toward the Caelian and the Arch of Constantine (Platner).

streets.name: Vicus Huiusce Diei (conjectural)
streets.modern: Palatine summit
streets.note: Street on the Palatine in Region X (Capitoline Base), perhaps named from a shrine of Fortuna Huiusce Diei.

streets.name: Vicus Fortunae Respicientis (conjectural)
streets.modern: south side of the Palatine above the Circus Maximus
streets.note: Street on the Palatine (Capitoline Base), perhaps on the south side, named from the shrine of Fortuna Respiciens (Notitia, Reg. X).

streets.name: Paved ring round the Colosseum
streets.modern: Piazza del Colosseo
streets.note: Travertine-paved belt about 17.5 m wide round the amphitheatre, bounded by stone bollards (cippi) for the awning ropes; modelled as an ellipse 12 m outside the 188 x 156 m facade, long axis ENE-WSW.

streets.name: Street behind the Basilica Iulia (Marble Plan)
streets.modern: south side of the Basilica Iulia
streets.note: Street along the back (south side) of the Basilica Iulia linking the Vicus Iugarius and the Vicus Tuscus, shown with the blocks behind it on the Severan Marble Plan.

streets.name: Street beside the Horrea Agrippiana
streets.modern: between the Vicus Tuscus and the Palatine slope
streets.note: Lane on the north side of the Horrea Agrippiana (Agrippa's warehouses) between the Vicus Tuscus and the foot of the Palatine.

streets.name: Street in front of the Hadrianeum
streets.modern: Via di Pietra - Piazza di Pietra
streets.note: Street from the Via Lata to the colonnade of the Temple of Divus Hadrianus (145), whose north flank stands in Piazza di Pietra.

streets.name: Street of the Forum Piscarium (fish market)
streets.modern: Via del Foro Piscario
streets.note: Lane by the Forum Piscarium, the fish market near the Porticus Octaviae and the river (Livy 40.51.5); medieval fish market (Pescheria) on the same spot.

streets.name: Road along the Claudian arches (tombs of the Statilii)
streets.modern: Via Statilia
streets.note: Ancient road beside the later arches of the Aqua Claudia toward the Porta Maggiore, lined with late Republican tombs (tomb of the Statilii); Via Statilia keeps its line.

streets.name: Street from the Circus Maximus carceres to the river (Via della Greca)
streets.modern: Via della Greca
streets.note: Short street from the starting gates of the Circus Maximus west along the foot of the Aventine to the Forum Boarium and the river (Ara Maxima, Statio Annonae).

streets.name: Vicus Drusianus (conjectural)
streets.modern: by the 'Arch of Drusus' inside the Porta Appia
streets.note: Street of Region I (Capitoline Base); placed near the arch traditionally called the Arch of Drusus on the Via Appia inside the later Porta Appia.

streets.name: Vicus Minervi (conjectural)
streets.modern: outside the Porta Pinciana, north-east (Via Po direction)
streets.note: Street of Region VII known from an altar to Stata Mater found just outside the Porta Pinciana; it may have run north-east from that gate (Platner).

streets.name: Road through the Horti Sallustiani
streets.modern: Via Sallustiana (approx.)
streets.note: Road through the valley of the imperial Horti Sallustiani between the Quirinal and the Pincian, on Via Sallustiana; the horti passed to the emperors under Tiberius.

streets.name: Vicus Ianuclensis (conjectural)
streets.modern: west slope of the Janiculum outside the Porta Aurelia
streets.note: Street of Region XIV (Capitoline Base), probably on the western slope of the Janiculum (Platner). Position illustrative.

streets.name: Street from the Pons Probi to the Via Ostiensis
streets.modern: near Piazza dell'Emporio / Via Marmorata
streets.note: Approach from the left-bank end of the Pons Probi (Probus, about 277; restored by Theodosius as Pons Theodosii) to the Via Ostiensis in the Emporium district.
